name: Coral reef
notes: Tropical reef and reef flat: no true land plants except on the adjoining cay/strand (coconut, naupaka, morning glory); the reef itself is built of coral, encrusting coralline algae, Halimeda and turf/sea-grape algae, with seagrass on the back-reef lagoon floor. Drawn on the Great Barrier Reef, Caribbean and Red Sea; underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Coconut palm

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

canopy.source: Palm of tropical coasts worldwide; height 15-30 m. Leaning trunk, feather crown; sea-dispersed nuts. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rare; most young trees arise when fallen branches or trunks root and sprout. Young stems are soft, thick and pale grey, with large, thin, bright pale-green oval leaves in loose pairs toward the shoot tips, making a leafy, open whip that soon forks into a spreading, soft-wooded tree.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 20 m in dense stands on coral cays; clusters of green sweet-smelling flowers; sticky barbed fruits spread on seabird feathers; frequent vegetative reproduction from fallen branches and basal shoots); growth rate and ages estimated from its soft, fast-growing wood

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (clusters of green, sweet-smelling flowers; sticky, barbed fruits that cling to seabird feathers); the fruit is a ribbed, glandular, one-seeded anthocarp about 1 cm long; timing, pollinators and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 oval cotyledons, then fleshy, glossy, bright-green spoon-shaped leaves crowded in a tuft at the shoot tip. Grows fast into a rounded, mounding shrub of thick, soft, pithy branches that sprawl over the sand and root where they touch, forming dense hedges along the beach.
growth.source: Wikipedia Scaevola taccada (3-10 m, branchlets 1-1.5 cm thick, leaves 8-25 cm; flowers all year; white fruit floats in seawater); Useful Tropical Plants/Hawaii native plant guides (slow, erratic germination of the corky stone, fast growth); ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Scaevola taccada: flowers all year in small axillary clusters, white 'half flowers' 2-2.5 cm with the 5 petal lobes fanned to one side, sometimes violet-streaked, pollinated by large bees or selfed; round fleshy drupe ripening green to white, corky stone floats in seawater; ripening time, set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings grow a single stout, pale stem topped by a loose rosette of large, fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves covered in silky silver hairs; after a year they are only ~35 cm tall. Branching comes later and sympodially, each shoot ending in a flat cluster of coiled white flower sprays, building the broad, rounded, silvery bush of the beach strand.
growth.source: Same species as Heliotropium arboreum (synonym; also Tournefortia argentea). Useful Tropical Plants (under 75 cm/yr, germination 2-4 weeks, seedlings ~35 cm after 12+ months); Hawaii-Pacific Weed Risk Assessment (4+ yr to reproduce, not shade tolerant); Plants of Hawaii. Lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Plants of Hawaii (drupe white, fleshy, globose ~4 mm, corky floating endocarp; corolla white 2.5-3.3 mm); Wikipedia (flowers ~0.6 cm); Useful Tropical Plants (flowers and fruits nearly all year; bees, butterflies). Ripening, hang and rot times, fruit set and crop estimated.

bark.note: submerged seagrass; rhizome and sheaths only

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds about 1 cm long are released when the ripe fruit splits and root within days on the sandy bottom. The seedling is a short shoot of 2-5 flat, bright-green ribbon leaves with rounded tips, anchored by a few thick roots; it grows a buried rhizome and after a year or two starts sending up new leaf shoots, spreading into a patch.
growth.source: Wikipedia Thalassia testudinum (leaves to 30 cm x 2 cm; rhizomes 5-10 cm deep; flowers Apr-Jul; fruit 20-25 mm with 1-6 seeds, splitting after ~8 weeks; low-tide mark to 30 m). Seed germination without dormancy, shoot lifespan (up to ~10-15 yr by leaf-scar ageing) and seedling-to-flowering time estimated from seagrass literature.
